hooks.notes: chat-layout.context.ts: {scrollContainer(), contentRef(el)}. Consumed here (the content element is registered with the layout, the scroll container roots the sentinel observer); provided by tct-chat-layout (WP-16), which imports the key from this folder.

keyboard.action: Focuses the log (tabindex 0 unless the author sets one)

differences.text: The log's native live region is off (role=log, aria-live=off). Upstream leaves it polite and relies on aria-busy to defer speech while streaming, which assistive technology honours inconsistently, so a stream is read token by token. The list instead announces each message once through the shared Announcer: while `streaming` nothing is spoken and the message is announced when it returns to false; without the flag a message is announced after 500 ms of quiet. Own (user) messages, history rows (inserted above the newest, or present at load) and all but the last of a batch larger than three are not announced; `no-announce` turns it off. `aria-busy` is also set while older messages load.

`focusLatestMessage()` and `no-announce` are additions. The list never moves focus or scrolls on its own; focusLatestMessage() is where the scroll button hands focus over. The messages are light-DOM children of the list; only the loading spinner, the spacer, the sentinel and the empty state are rendered in its shadow root.

The spacer cancels the row gap that follows it (negative margin), so a list that fills its container starts at the same place with either alignment; upstream leaves one extra gap above the first row in `bottom` mode.

requests.reason: tct-chat-layout provides chatLayoutContext (chat-message-list/chat-layout.context.ts) and wires ChatStreamScrollController and ChatNewMessagesController: scroller = its scroll container; ChatNewMessagesController.contentRef = the context's contentRef; onResize = scroll.scrollIfLocked(). Its message area must not shrink below its content (flex: 1 0 auto), or the list stops growing with its messages and the resize observer never fires. The scroll button takes visible = scroll.isScrolledUp || news.hasNewMessages and label = "New messages" (@astryx.chatLayout.newMessages) while news.hasNewMessages; its click calls news.dismiss() and scroll.scrollToBottom(). chat-stream.test.ts holds a working harness.
Import the token types (ChatToken, ChatTokenBadge, ChatTokenCustom) from chat-message/chat-message.types.ts for ChatComposerToken, and share the ChatComposerToken to tct-chat-tokenized-text shape.

hooks.notes: chat-stream-scroll.ts. {isScrolledUp, isLocked, scrollToBottom({behavior}), scrollToMessage, scrollToLastMessage, lock, unlock, scrollIfLocked}. Spring follow with reduced-motion jump, reader-wins unlock from position, first fill instant, scroll anchoring off while following.

keyboard.action: Reaches the button only while it is visible (hidden: inert, visibility hidden); never the first tab stop at rest

differences.text: Focus is not lost when the button hides while it holds focus: it moves to `focusTarget`, else the newest message of the nearest tct-chat-message-list (focusLatestMessage()), after the scroll the button asked for. Hidden is `inert` as well as `visibility: hidden`, so it is out of the tab order and the accessibility tree immediately, not at the end of the fade.

The pill takes the default padding of tct-button (no padding hook; `--radius-element` is set to the full radius on the inner button). The host lets clicks through outside the pill (pointer-events: none), where upstream sets it on the dock.

useChatStreamScroll and useChatNewMessages are Lit reactive controllers. `scrollend` re-locking has a debounced-scroll fallback that also runs where scrollend exists (the handler is idempotent), because feature probes belong to core/features.ts (a shared file; see requests). `overflow-anchor: none` on the following container is an adopted stylesheet rule on an attribute, so the consumer's own value is never read or written (as upstream's injected <style>).

A reader's upward move that has not produced its scroll event yet wins over a resize-driven write of ours (the reduced-motion jump in particular would otherwise put the position back before the reader's scroll was ever seen); the spring ends on the exact bottom pixel instead of stalling one or two pixels short.

requests.reason: Optional: add a `scrollEnd` probe (`'onscrollend' in window`) so ChatStreamScrollController can skip its debounced-scroll settle timer where the engine fires scrollend (Safari < 26.2 lacks it). The controller is correct without it, so nothing is blocked.
